newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean agent says infiltration into S.Korea easy.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean agent says infiltration into S.Korea easy.

text.p: The only North Korean captured alive after landing from a grounded submarine last month said on Monday his team had faced little difficulty sneaking in past South Korean coastal defences.
"If you come in by a submarine you can do it as many times as you like," Lee Kwang-soo told a news conference, his first meeting with the South Korean media since he was captured on September 18.
Lee said the North Korean submarine was on a reconnaissance mission, contradicting North Korean assertions that it had drifted into Southern waters after developing engine trouble.
He said he overheard a colleague on board the vessel boasting that he had sneaked into South Korea three times.
Tensions have been high on the Korean peninsula since the submarine landed 26 North Koreans on an east coast beach. All but three of the infiltrators have been killed or captured.
Lee said his Shark-class submarine passed a South Korean navy vessel equipped with with sonar detectors.
"We could evade it with ease," he said.
